source.title: On the Maximum Hessian Eigenvalue and Generalization
source.authors: Simran Kaur; Jérémy E. Cohen; Zachary Chase Lipton

record.file_problem: none; full paper text including appendix is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own SGD training experiments on CIFAR-10 and states that several model setups were trained until reaching 99% training accuracy, but it does not test the claim's random-initialization or label-corruption conditions.
record.gate_note: The 99% training-accuracy target is a stopping condition stated for the experiments; the paper does not separately report achieved training accuracy by run or condition. Results about test accuracy and λmax do not measure the claim versions' stated training outcomes or training speed.
record.test_reason: The study uses a 99% training-accuracy stopping criterion to compare sharpness and generalization. It does not report training-error outcomes independently of that criterion, training speed, or loss trajectories relative to an initial stability threshold. Its own results primarily concern generalization and Hessian sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that smaller maximum Hessian eigenvalues do not reliably explain improved generalization: several interventions reduce this eigenvalue without improving test accuracy, while BN can improve test accuracy without reducing it. They explicitly restrict this conclusion to this flatness metric.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies Hessian sharpness and generalization across training interventions; it reports CIFAR-10 runs stopped at 99% train accuracy but does not test the full claim recipe, including random or corrupted labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Generalization and λmax vary with batch size, learning rate, SAM penalty, dropout probability, and batch normalization; these are not reported as changing the 99% training-accuracy target.

fits_no_version.finding: Learning rate, batch size, SAM, and dropout can reduce the maximum Hessian eigenvalue without improving generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The maximum Hessian eigenvalue is not a reliable generalization predictor across these training interventions.

fits_no_version.finding: BN changes test accuracy while producing similar sharpness at fixed learning rate and batch size; its generalization benefit depends on learning rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BN can improve generalization without reducing maximum Hessian eigenvalue.

fits_no_version.finding: Large-batch VGG solutions have final maximum Hessian eigenvalues approximately equal to 2/eta.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Final sharpness in these large-batch experiments tracks the learning-rate stability threshold.

record.code_released: https://github.com/davda54/sam (SAM implementation used; paper code release not stated)
record.problems: For the training-error claim, 99% train accuracy is reported as a stopping criterion rather than as per-run outcomes; initialization details and corrupted-label conditions are not reported. Several relevant plots report test accuracy and λmax, not the training-error result.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained: the paper's other training-to-99%-accuracy descriptions overlap the reported setup categories, and its figures focus on test accuracy and λmax rather than reporting separate training-error values.

untested.parts: Independent training-error outcomes, random-initialization conditions, corrupted or random labels, CIFAR-100, and effects of model size, early stopping, or regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-minimum frequencies, and extra student neurons.
Training-error comparisons across depth, identity shortcuts, longer training, and special initialization.
Initialization comparisons, signal or gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.

Initial stability limits, transient loss increases and recovery, divergence boundaries, and simultaneous full-batch sharpness and falling-loss trajectories. Final sharpness near 2/eta does not establish those dynamics.
Accuracy gained per training time or iteration, comparative learning-rate tolerance, and matched Fixup versus normalization training-speed and stability comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The training descriptions suggest that retained runs reached the stopping threshold, but do not establish success rates across attempted runs. Treating that selection criterion as an independently measured outcome would overstate the evidence.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports CIFAR-10 models trained to a 99% training-accuracy threshold, but does not state that initialization was random, test corrupted or random labels, compare model sizes, or study early stopping and regularization.
